Configure agents for consumers at scale to report violations to regulators. Wait time not accurate or communicated? Complaint filed. Human agent not available within time limit? Complaint filed.

Think about all the time and effort for all of the consumers in the aggregate that would be needed to hold corporate counter parties accountable, with the cost being code and some compute time on device. This is where AI agents shine. They can do the mundane work of capturing evidence of compliance violations, time stamping, packaging the violation event, and shipping to an endpoint for reporting them.

Every consumer’s phone becomes a regulator watchdog node. We can even use LLMs to rapidly ship the app(s) needed to do this.

children.author: redrix
children.text:
Some of the best uses of AI in call centres that I’ve seen focus on improving human interaction instead of getting rid of it. For example:

- Finding information in the background / performing an account health check instead of putting the caller on hold for 20 minutes.

- Helping newer consultants find the same offers experienced staff know about amongst 200 pages of active/targeted offers.

- Automatically documenting calls so when someone calls back, they don’t get a “sorry, I can’t find any notes about that on your account”.

- Giving the offshore call center consultant a customized script based on the active discussion instead of a generic one

(Yes, reading from a script is still bad, but at least this makes it somewhat more natural rather than it feeling like you’re talking to a lobotomised employee.)
